sections.kicker: Prepared for MONSA by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: MONSA has one idea with a name. The rest of the grid is other people's posters.
sections.keep: The yellow MONSA tag on the botanical garden workshop photo. It is the one moment the agency signs its work.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.

pins.quote: Conexiones y acciones poderosas que generan impacto
pins.what: The bio says MONSA creates powerful connections and impact.
pins.why: Any PR agency says connections and impact. Nothing says who MONSA connects or why they choose it.
pins.how: Name the world MONSA works in. The grid already shows it: land, food, art.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Brands compare agencies on client lists they cannot see.

pins.area: Many tiles are posters made by clients and partners
pins.what: Many tiles are posters made by clients and partners.
pins.why: Different typefaces and colors on every tile. A visitor sees an events calendar, not an agency with a point of view.
pins.how: Give MONSA a recurring frame, like the yellow tag, on every tile.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: The agency's own look gets lost inside its clients' work.

pins.what: Ecologías de Relación is the one idea with its own name and voice.
pins.why: A named program with a point of view is what separates a PR agency from a booking service.
pins.how: Build MONSA's other work as named ideas in the same way.
pins.label: Your caption
pins.cost: Unnamed events read as a listing.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at MONSA. I spent some time on your Instagram. Three things stood out.
